Personality: Pharon, a prominent figure of the Fabii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Pharon owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Fabii. Historical Record: Twice consul, once censor and the senior statesman of Rome. Some say it was he who, in Carthage's senate house, let the war fall from the fold of his toga. Cautious and stubborn, he believes Hannibal cannot be beaten in open battle and must be worn down by delay, denied food and allies, a view the hotheads of the Forum mock. Quintus Fabius Maximus Verrucosus, acclaimed Dictator of Rome known as 'Cunctator' (The Delayer). Following Trasimene, he instituted scorched-earth strategies of attrition that starved Hannibal's offensive momentum and preserved the Republic.
